```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Faster path to a first payment. A's buyer grants a survey widget access to order data. B's buyer must trust a solo operator with bank and payment data, which B's own brief says carries SOC2 expectations (a licensed CPA audit), migration support and tax-season support that one person with agents can hardly deliver in 90 days.",
    "Lighter compliance before launch. A needs a one-time privacy and DPA review plus Shopify app review. B needs ongoing SOC2-type assurance, Stripe and Plaid terms review, and financial-PII privacy work.",
    "Built-in discovery. A ships into the Shopify App Store, a self-serve marketplace where merchants already search for this category. B's Stripe App Marketplace is also free distribution, but B's paid fallback is finance search, where clicks can exceed $50. A's quoted ~$6 CPC is a more workable cost for a cheap test.",
    "Sourced proof that a solo founder can win this exact model. A cites an Indie Hackers post on Zigpoll reaching $125K MRR as a solo founder. B shows lean competitors at $29–$100/mo but no comparable sourced solo-founder outcome.",
    "Narrower build. A's scope (checkout survey, exit-intent popup, dashboard, Klaviyo/Flow integrations) is tighter and lower-risk than bookkeeping and reconciliation, where errors carry financial consequences."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's most concrete value claim, that Growthy estimates $400–600/mo in bookkeeper time per Stripe-connected client, has no source link and counts as missing. Two other gaps compound it. Part of the competitor list ('Fynance, Cosmly, ReInvestWealth, HelloBooks.ai') is unsourced and attributed only to a 'kill-gate's own list'. And Kick's free tier is described inconsistently: 'up to 250 txns/yr' in one place and 'up to $25K/mo expenses' in another.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low. B actually has stronger demand evidence: three independent sourced quotes, one with a quantified 3–4 hours per month. A rests on a single Reddit merchant quote plus a competitor's origin story. A's claim that rejecting manual outreach shows willingness to pay is an inference, not evidence. Both markets are saturated with free tiers, and A's own brief notes Zigpoll took two years to gain traction. A wins mainly because B's trust and compliance barriers look more likely to block a paying customer within 90 days, not because A's demand is better proven."
}
```
